publications.title: Zero Filling and Persistent Free Subgroups of the Figure-Eight Knot
publications.description:
The figure-eight knot gives a negative answer to the literal universal rank-two free-subgroup question printed on p.493 of Motegi's Oberwolfach Report 8/2020 contribution. It is hyperbolic and has no finite nonmeridional surgery, but every free rank-two subgroup has a nontrivial element killed by zero filling. The zero filling is a torus bundle, so its metabelian fundamental group kills an explicit nontrivial second-derived word. The short proof verifies the no-finite-surgery hypothesis across all rational slopes using the credited classical filling classification. Rational slopes include zero and exclude the meridian at infinity.

The topology and group-law ingredients are classical; related algebra in Boden-Friedl and earlier Ito-Motegi-Teragaito text is credited. The result refutes a universal affirmative assertion and leaves the separate search for a positive hyperbolic example unresolved. Two independent primary-source priority audits found no earlier explicit full counterexample in inspected text, but priority cannot be fully cleared. The full 2024 cyclic-persistence and 2019 vanishing-elements bodies were not inspected, and some longer precursors were scanned and selectively read. No historical-first, new-topology or continued-open-status claim is made. A historical precursor's subsequently acknowledged Claim6.3 gap is disclosed; that claim is not a proof dependency. The authored-only verification package preserves 22 original inputs, independent derivations and reviews, source read scopes and hashes, exact finite controls, nested manifests and an offline replay driver. A pinned exact-inventory gate repairs a historical release verifier's unanchored manifest and constant source-exclusion flag without changing original evidence. Raw third-party sources and account data are excluded. Finite checks supplement the proof; integrity is not authenticity or priority.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, research, writing, reproduction and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with internal AI adversarial reviews; it has not received human peer review or proof-assistant certification.

publications.title: A Minimal-Surface Counterexample to a Seshadri Lower Bound
publications.description:
For every integer d at least 7, a classical integral plane pencil followed by a double base change gives a smooth minimal complex projective surface S with ample canonical bundle, K_S^2=6(d-1)(d-3), and an ample integral line bundle L with L^2=6 and epsilon(S,L;x) at most 1/(d-1). This strictly contradicts the proposed bound 1/(2+|K_S^2|^(1/4)) in Szemberg's 2007/2008 question, repeated as OWR21/2009 Conjecture2 and Primer-v2 Question6.1.6. The d=7 witness has K_S^2=144, polarization degree1 on the exhibited curve, and point multiplicity6. The proof supplies finite-degree pencil existence, all-curve ampleness, smoothness, connectedness, minimality and the degree-one lifted singular fibre. The additive2 is outside the fourth root, correcting a catalogue transcription.

Miranda's pencil and polarization are credited through Ein-Lazarsfeld1993, Bauer1999 and Bauer-Szemberg2010 Proposition2.1; the cover and positivity ingredients are classical. Two independent primary-source priority audits found no explicit earlier exact resolution in inspected text, but priority cannot be fully cleared. The full Bansal-Majumder2025 survey, Roy2019 thesis and other thesis bodies were not inspected; longer sources and citation bodies were selectively read and final journal versions were not globally compared. No firstness, new-method or verified continued-open-status claim is made. Only an upper Seshadri bound at a special point on varying surfaces is asserted, not an exact value, fixed-surface vanishing, rank-one or very-general-point violation. The authored-only package preserves18 original inputs, independent derivations and source receipts, four review families, pinned inventories, exact symbolic controls and a nine-job offline replay driver. SymPy1.14.0 and mpmath1.3.0 must be preinstalled. Raw third-party documents and account data are excluded. Finite controls supplement the geometric proof; integrity is not authenticity or priority.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, research, writing, source comparison, reproduction and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with internal AI adversarial reviews; it has not received human peer review or proof-assistant certification.

publications.title: A relation-incidence proof of Tohăneanu's low-exponent supersolvability conjecture
publications.description: Every finite central free hyperplane arrangement over a characteristic-zero field whose nonzero exponents are 1 or 2 with at most one 3 is supersolvable. This research note proves the full conjecture in Tohăneanu's Oberwolfach contribution using linear-relation formality, rank-two counts, a forced K4 incidence core and modular terminal-pencil extensions. The paper credits the earlier all-2, tree, rank-three and modular-pruning results and acknowledges Ferudun's matching October 12, 2026 preprint. The verification archive preserves the October 4 PR candidate and dated disclosure records, source/priority audits and reproducible exact computational diagnostics. No exhaustive first-priority or independent-development claim is made. AI tools were used extensively in solving, writing and verifying the work. This is an unrefereed preprint; internal AI reviews do not constitute independent human peer review.

publications.title: Forward generation does not ensure GNS descent: an explicit continuous counterexample
publications.description: Generation by an observed algebra and its forward translates does not ensure descent through a general dilation's fixed expectation-GNS representation. This research note constructs a unital separable, injective, point-norm continuous C*-dilation of the two-state exponential relaxation semigroup, exactly forward-generated by C2. Its GNS image is M2, and an explicit nonzero positive kernel element leaves the kernel at every positive time. This refutes the concrete generation-only proposal in Skeide's 2009 module-approach problem. The clock/evaluation/cocycle mechanism is credited to Burgarth, Facchi and Hillier; the negative phenomenon is also a short unstated corollary of their earlier clock model. Finite-unitary and first-derivative antecedents are credited to Dive, Mintert and Burgarth and to vom Ende. No new general dilation method or literature-first priority is claimed. Stronger minimality conditions and extension after separately imposed kernel invariance remain outside the result. The verification archive preserves the original PR candidate, independent analytic audits, primary-source attribution evidence and reproducible exact checks. AI tools were used extensively in construction, writing and verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; internal AI reviews do not constitute human peer review.
